title: 04. LangChain & Frameworks: Day 8 — LangChain Fundamentals: Build 2 Productivity Agents
summary: Welcome to Phase 2. For the last seven days you lived inside Pydantic AI.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Welcome to Phase 2. For the last seven days you lived inside Pydantic AI. Now we widen the lens: you will spend the next fourteen days building productivity agents across **LangChain**, **LangGraph**, and **Pydantic AI**. Today is your LangChain on-ramp. LangChain shines for productivity work because it gives you composable, pipe-able primitives (prompts, models, parsers) that turn a one-off LLM call into a repeatable pipeline. By the end of this file you will have triaged an inbox and summarized a meeting transcript, both in under 100 lines each.

sections.title: LangChain Building Blocks (Quick Reference)
sections.body:
LangChain's core abstraction is the **Runnable** — anything with `.invoke()`, `.batch()`, and `.stream()`. You compose Runnables with the pipe operator `|` to form an **LCEL chain** (LangChain Expression Language). The pieces you will use today:

- **`ChatOpenAI`** — a chat model wrapper. Pass `model="gpt-4o-mini"` and `temperature`. It is itself a Runnable.
- **`ChatPromptTemplate`** — builds message lists from a template string and variables. Use `from_messages([...])` with `("system", ...)`, `("human", ...)` tuples.
- **`PydanticOutputParser`** — wraps a Pydantic model, injects format instructions into the prompt, and parses the model's text into the typed object.
- **`with_structured_output(...)`** — a shortcut on chat models that uses function-calling under the hood instead of prompt-injected instructions. Often cleaner than `PydanticOutputParser`.
- **LCEL chain** — `prompt | model | parser`. Each step's output feeds the next. `chain.invoke({...})` runs it; `chain.batch([...])` runs it in parallel.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
- **Forgetting `.partial(...)` on the prompt.** If you put `{format_instructions}` in the template but never `.partial()` it, every `.invoke()` will fail with a missing-variable error. Either `.partial()` at build time or pass it in each invoke call.
- **Using `Enum` without `str` mixin.** `class Category(Enum)` serializes to `{"value": "Urgent"}` in JSON schema — the model often returns the wrong shape. Always use `class Category(str, Enum)`.
- **Mixing `PydanticOutputParser` with `with_structured_output`.** They do similar things via different mechanisms. If you use both, the model gets conflicting instructions (one saying "respond as JSON", the other forcing a function call). Pick one per chain.
- **`batch()` on a non-thread-safe parser.** Most parsers are fine, but if you wrap a custom parser around shared mutable state, parallel batches race. Keep parsers stateless.
- **`temperature=0` does not mean deterministic across API versions.** OpenAI's `gpt-4o-mini` still drifts a few percent between calls. For tests, mock the model with a fake Runnable that returns a canned `AIMessage`.
- **Forgetting to load `.env`.** `ChatOpenAI()` reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment. If you forget `load_dotenv()`, you get a cryptic `AuthenticationError` with no obvious cause.

sections.title: What's Next
sections.body: LangChain's LCEL chains are linear: data flows top-to-bottom through `prompt | model | parser`. But real productivity agents need **branching** — route this email to a drafter, that one to spam, this one to a calendar invite parser. That's where **LangGraph** comes in. Tomorrow (Day 9) you will build a `StateGraph` with conditional edges, run a multi-node task router, and implement a human-in-the-loop standup generator with a regeneration loop. See you there.
